The Best Way to Keep Pet Hair Under Control at Home

If you live with a dog or cat, completely hair-free furniture is not a realistic goal. A better strategy is to keep shedding from building into thick layers by combining grooming, washable fabrics, regular vacuuming, and targeted cleanup.

The Quick Answer

Vacuum high-traffic areas regularly, use a rubber hair-removal tool on fabric where appropriate, wash pet bedding routinely, and concentrate effort on favorite sleeping spots. Choose vacuum attachments based on the surface instead of using maximum suction everywhere.

Materials Needed

- Vacuum with floor and upholstery attachments
- Rubber pet-hair tool
- Microfiber cloths
- Lint roller
- Washable blankets or pet covers

Step-by-Step Routine

1. Start with furniture
Remove loose hair from couches and chairs before vacuuming the floor so fallen hair can be collected afterward.

2. Clean pet bedding
Wash bedding according to its care label. Removing hair before washing can reduce the amount that ends up in the machine.

3. Vacuum slowly
Use overlapping passes on carpet and the appropriate attachment on hard floors.

4. Detail edges
Baseboards, stairs, under furniture, and corners often collect hair that a large floor head misses.

5. Protect favorite spots
A washable throw on a pet's favorite couch area can make weekly maintenance much easier.

What NOT to Do

- Do not use tools that snag delicate upholstery.
- Do not soak fabric while trying to remove hair.
- Do not ignore the vacuum brush roll when hair wraps around it.
- Do not use a cleaner without checking carpet or upholstery care instructions.

US Home Tips Generic Guides Miss

The best routine depends on the home. In apartments, prioritize the sofa, bedroom, and main traffic path rather than trying to deep-clean every room daily. In larger homes, zone the work across the week. A washable cover can be more effective than repeatedly deep-cleaning a couch.

Maintenance Tips

Vacuum high-shedding zones several times a week, wash pet bedding regularly, and groom pets according to appropriate veterinary or grooming guidance.

FAQ

How do I remove pet hair before vacuuming?
A rubber hair-removal tool can gather loose hair from some carpets and fabrics before vacuuming. Test it first on delicate materials.

Why does pet hair collect under furniture?
Air movement, static, and normal shedding move lightweight hair into edges and low spaces.

Should I vacuum every day?
High-shedding homes may benefit from frequent quick passes, but the ideal schedule depends on pets, flooring, and household traffic.
